title: Official blog admission stage 11
summary: This iteration makes the OpenAI and Anthropic official-blog admission threshold explicit and reusable by internal artifacts. Preview, intake, context, and knowledge-index outputs now carry a versioned policy that tells later AI review to use only the title plus capped opening preview for first-pass triage, include durable product/model/engineering knowledge, exclude ordinary company news, and route technical customer or partnership stories to review instead of automatic curation.

validation_commands: node --test --test-name-pattern "official blog admission policy|official blog intake CLI|official blog context CLI" tests/official-blog-knowledge.test.js tests/unit.test.js

lessons.lesson: Official-blog intake needs to carry the admission standard as data, not only source-code behavior.
lessons.evidence: Stage 11 adds `admission_policy.version`, `first_pass`, `include_criteria`, `exclude_categories`, and `review_rule` to internal preview, intake, context, and knowledge-index artifacts.
lessons.recommended_action: Use the policy artifact as the prompt contract when a later stage asks an AI reviewer to decide whether a new OpenAI or Anthropic post belongs in the curated knowledge graph.

lessons.lesson: First-pass blog admission should stay preview-only until a candidate is reviewed.
lessons.evidence: The policy records title plus opening preview as the only first-pass input and keeps the existing two-paragraph, 1200-character cap.
lessons.recommended_action: Do not let downstream AI review use full article text for the initial include/exclude decision; use full reading only after an item reaches review or authoring.

lessons.lesson: Public official-blog output should expose curation scope, not internal admission mechanics.
lessons.evidence: Stage 11 tests prove `toPublicOfficialBlogKnowledge` omits `admission_policy`, `first_pass`, and `company_news` internals while preserving the public curation scope.
lessons.recommended_action: Keep internal policy details in local artifacts; public pages should show curated records and reader-safe scope only.

suggestions.issue: The official-blog admission standard could drift between deterministic intake, AI review, and future daily-generation prompts because internal artifacts only exposed results, not the rule used to produce them.
suggestions.evidence: Stage 11 adds a schema-validated versioned admission policy and asserts it on pure functions plus CLI outputs.
suggestions.suggestion: Carry `official-blog-admission-v1` with internal official-blog artifacts and require later AI reviewers to follow the preview-only include/exclude/review rule.
suggestions.expected_benefit: New blog intake, translation, and daily-context steps can consistently reject low-value company news while preserving high-value product, model, and engineering-practice posts.
suggestions.promotion_path: Implemented through schema-validated internal policy metadata and deterministic tests.
validation_evidence: official blog admission policy is versioned and preview-only for internal artifacts
public official blog knowledge exposes curation scope without internal admission policy details
official blog intake CLI writes a clean internal review queue
official blog context CLI writes clean internal context

followups.action: When wiring official-blog intake into daily generation, include the policy artifact next to the review queue so AI review uses the same preview-only admission standard.
Add real-feed examples for OpenAI and Anthropic after live intake is wired, but keep tests deterministic with stored fixtures.
